messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Error in Biogeo
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Nick,

Yes, it was a path issue. In case others have this problem:

For a Mac
In the pdf/plot portion of the sample, I changed
scriptdir = np(system.file("~path", package="BioGeoBEARS"))
to
scriptdir = np(system.file("extdata/a_scripts", package="BioGeoBEARS"))
Basically just shortening the path let the machine figure out the folders location and call the cornercoords script.

Thanks again!
Jon

messages.subject: Can I add 95% HPD intervals to nodes on the phylogeny in R?
messages.subject_clean: Can I add 95% HPD intervals to nodes on the phylogeny in R?
messages.body_plain:
Can I add 95% HPD intervals to nodes on the phylogeny in R?

Being very new to the BioGeoBEARS package I might have overlooked something, and I am not sure if this is the right forum to ask.

But is there a way to add the 95% HPD intervals around the nodes in the phylogeny in R after I have inferred the biogeographic history with BioGeoBEARS?

Even though this R-code http://phylo.wikidot.com/beastmaster#tipdate_plots_script_code <http://phylo.wikidot.com/beastmaster%23tipdate_plots_script_code>

should be able to plot the 95% HPD intervals, it looks to me like it needs the log-files from the BEAST-run to do this, or at least a summary of the log-file from Tracer.

But I am wondering whether this is making the process even more complicated, and also, I do not have the log-files any longer. They took up too much space.

I guess, I could rerun the BEAST analysis to recreate the log-files, but I find this slightly unnecessary as my tree-file already have the information about the 95% HPD intervals.

I can visualize the 95%HPD intervals in FigTree 1.4.

I could copy the tree in a graphical format, and rescale it and overlay it in illustrator or similar software that can work with vector graphics. But it would be nice to be able to do this regularly with a code in R.

It gets annoying when I have to do it again and again.

I discovered that this package:

http://www.christophheibl.de/Rpackages.html

and the associated tar.gz files dowloaded and placed locally:

phyloch_1.5-3.tgz

strap_1.4.tar.gz

geoscale_2.0.tar.gz

And having installed all the necessary packages in R.

"phyloch"

"strap"

"geoscale"

"OutbreakTools"

"ape"

"colorspace"

"XML"

"phytools"

"paleotree"

"phylobase"

And this code :

my_tree <- read.annotated.nexus("my_beast_test.tre")

Will read in my phylogenetic tree in to R, and I can check that all rates and heights and lengths and 95%HPD intervals are in this element:

my_tree [6]

On this webpage:

http://nickcrouch.github.io/r_pages/add_HPD_info/add.HPD.info.html

It looks like I can plot the 95% HPD intervals, if I can extract the upper and lower values for each 95% HPD interval for each node in my tree.

But I do not know how to extract this information from the object ‘my_tree’ I created above.

With the phylobase package:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/phylobase/index.html

And following the examples here:

https://artax.karlin.mff.cuni.cz/r-help/library/phylobase/html/as-methods.html

I found, that I can prepare a dataframe in R that holds the information in my input tree in columns.

The columns in the dataframe appears to hold the information I can see in:

my_tree [5]

my_tree [4]

my_tree [3]

my_tree [2]

my_tree [1]

But not the information in

my_tree [6]

I suspect this would require additional subdivision of the elements nested in my_tree [6]

My guess is that if I could add all the elements I have in “my_tree [6]” to the dataframe I produced with the phylobase package.

I would have what I need to complete the parts described here:

http://nickcrouch.github.io/r_pages/add_HPD_info/add.HPD.info.html

But I am not sure how to do this.

Can anyone help me work this one out?

The ultimate goal is of course to use both the features in the BioGeoBEARS package to get the biogeographic history as pie charts on the nodes, and have the 95% HPD intervals on each node.

And finally use the phyloch package to add a geological time scale underneath.

This code here below makes a pretty geological time scale for the tree I have attached to this question, by using the phyloch package.

geoscalePhylo(tree=my_tree, units=c("Period", "Epoch", "Age"), direction="rightwards", boxes="Epoch", cex.tip=0.5, cex.age=0.7, cex.ts=0.7, label.offset=0, x.lim=c(-40,150), lwd=3, width=2)

Thanks in advance for your time and help

messages.body_plain:
[I just read the "too many pie charts" thread, my question is a follow up to this]

I have  a big tree so is there a way to increase the distance between the branches in the Y-axis? (similar to the Expansion in FigTree)

As you said before one can just plot only some nodes of interest, but in this case I thing I could fit everything if I could just scale the total height of the figure. I will additionally export as a pdf -avoiding the default 8.5x11- and resize it a little through Rstudio but first I think the "Expansion" would help too.

Also, is there a way to avoid using the names -or code for regions- inside the square at each node (so every square is the same size regardless the combination of tags describing the composite area)?

Thanks for your help
best

Andrés

I will additionally export as a pdf -avoiding the default 8.5x11- and resize it a little through Rstudio but first I think the "Expansion" would help too.
>
> Also, is there a way to avoid using the names -or code for regions- inside the square at each node (so every square is the same size regardless the combination of tags describing the composite area)?
>

Hi,

These options are not available, nor would they be easy to do. The BioGeoBEARS plot function is just making use of APE's plot.phylo etc., and has similar constraints.

For those wanting to do non-default plots, the main thing I can recommend is type:

plot_BioGeoBEARS_results

...look at the code within this function, and you will see how the default plots are made with basic APE functions.  Modifying this code will allow you to do more, but anything really fancy will be a matter of either Adobe Illustrator & manual editing, or some elaborate effort at writing huge new functions.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Fully-sampled phylogenies and BioGeoBears
messages.body_plain:
Re-sending from correct email...

Hi Jenna!  I'm not sure where you heard that, but BioGeoBEARS does *not* incorporate incomplete taxon sampling.  Instead, BioGeoBEARS is in effect assuming that whatever tree you input is the complete tree.  Similarly, it is ignoring extinction (lineage extinction, not extinction-as-loss-of-a-range). This is why I caution against e.g. genus-level analyses:

OTUs of the phylogeny should be species/populations, not genera or other higher clades
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#genus_trees

Incorporating it is imaginable but would require using an SSE approach from e.g. diversitree, but these seem to be fairly tightly limited by computational time as they use numerical integration. I have some ideas about how to make this more feasible for large state spaces but that's a large project that is a ways off.

In Matzke (2014), I did do a bunch of simulations that indicated that missing extinct species did not have a dramatic impact on results, at least in the case I tested (random extinction), but of course heavily nonrandom extinction or nonrandom incomplete sampling could have huge effects (and would on almost any sort of phylogenetic comparative method, probably even methods explicitly designed to deal with incomplete sampling...dealing successfully with systematic processes that remove data from the dataset in a biased way is very very hard).

You may be thinking of the detection probability model (published only in my PhD at the moment), but this is designed mostly for fossil data.  Extinct lineages are usable, if they are in the tree (e.g. a tip-dated tree), but this is a different thing from a formal model that formally takes into account missing species due to extinction or incomplete sampling.

So, on the upside -- complete sampling is GOOD, and it seems like you have that, so you should be good to go!
Cheers, Nick

messages.body_plain:
Hi -- the PDF could be empty if e.g. you accidentally opened a PDF earlier with the pdf() command but didn't close it with dev.off().  I would suggest re-running the script, but set runslow=FALSE if the likelihood search took a long time to avoid repeating that.

Cheers!
